newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Norilsk names Interrosimpeks sole exporter.
newsitem.headline: Russian Norilsk names Interrosimpeks sole exporter.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel metals group NKEL.RTS 0#NKEL.RUO has named Russia-based Interrosimpeks its sole authorised exporter and foreign agent, a Norilsk spokesman said on Monday.
Sergei Vetchinin said Interrosimpeks had handled 97 percent of Norilsk's nickel exports since July.
He said London-based Normaco Ltd, a Norilsk subsidiary, was carrying out previously-concluded contracts but Norilsk was not awarding Normaco new contracts to sell nickel or copper.
Normaco officials were unavailable for comment.
Interrosimpeks is part of the Interros financial-industrial group controlled by Norilsk and Uneximbank, which has a 38 percent stake in RAO Norilsky Nikel.

"Since July, the breakdown of metal exports by Normaco and Interrosimpeks has been as follows -- about three percent of nickel and 7.4 percent of copper though Normaco," Vetchinin told Reuters. "The rest went through Interrosimpeks.
"Interrosimpeks is not only the chief exporter but also the trade agent."
Vetchinin said Norilsk would work with Normaco again only when Normaco took on financing and marketing roles.
"We are not satisfied with the role of Normaco as a simple registrar of deals," he said. "We want Normaco to be a complete marketing enterprise... in charge of getting credits and prefinancing."
But he said Norilsk hoped Normaco and Interrosimpeks would work together.
"We plan for Interrosimpeks to be the main, exclusive exporter and for Normaco to be the exclusive foreign agent. Normaco will distribute metal to the end-user and to traders," he said.
A Norilsk statement said new contracts conducted through Interrosimpeks were more profitable.

"Additional profit to Norilsk Nickel for sales of metal through Interrosimpeks are 1.8 percent (of average spot London Metals Exchange prices) for nickel and 3.1 percent for copper, or an additional $130 per tonne of nickel and $62 per tonne of copper," it said.
Vetchinin said Norilsk would move to selling directly to end-users.
"The strategic goal of Interrosimpeks as foreign agent of Norilsk is to supply the end-user -- firms like (Fried) Krupp AG, Thyssen AG," he said.
"But today Interrosimpeks works with traders as well because traders will pre-finance -- we must work with traders because of our present severe lack of working capital."
The Norilsk group produced 180,100 tonnes of nickel in 1995 and sees 1996 production rising three percent. It sees copper production up six percent on 1995's 338,700 tonnes.
Vetchinin said Interrosimpeks could expand its role.
"Ideally Interrosimpeks brings the metal to Normaco, and Normaco takes the metal to the foreign market...If that doesn't work Interrosimpeks will open up its offices abroad," he said.
--Peter Henderson, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
